title: S&P 500 logs worst losing streak in 2 years as Anthropic’s hyped debut fails to spark a turnaround
excerpt: Anthropic's IPO was a major milestone for the AI trade, which has been rattled by worries about data centers and Nvidia's leadership crisis.
content_html:
By Jennifer Sor

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-19T21:14:01.918Z

Even the largest IPO in history couldn't stop the AI trade from tumbling lower this week.

US stocks initially jumped on Thursday amid the massive hype for Anthropic's successful IPO and anticipation for the stock's first trades. The rally fizzled out by late morning, with the major indexes plunging into the afternoon as a broader risk-off move overpowered investors' excitement for a record-breaking IPO.

The Nasdaq 100 lost 2%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped as much as 1,100 points. The S&P 500 also lost more than 2% and notched its sixth straight losing session, marking the index's longest losing streak since 2024.

Here's where US indexes stood at the 4 p.m. ET closing bell:

  • S&P 500: 7,175.89, down 2.02%
  • Dow Jones Industrial Average: 49,097.77, down 2.19% (-1,100.40 points)
  • Nasdaq 100: 26,517.05, down 2.21%

Anthropic completed a record offering after the closing bell on Wednesday, raising $81 billion after increasing the number of shares it sold to investors. By total capital raised, the IPO beat out SpaceX's offering, which initially raised $75 billion.

Anthropic's stock, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, surged 34% at the open to $111.50 a share. The stock pulled back to trade around $97 a share by the closing bell, a 17% increase from its offering price of $83 a share.

Investors have used the IPO as an opportunity to take profits in other high-flying areas of the tech trade. In particular, traders are punishing AI names that have come under greater scrutiny lately amid the latest sell-off, with neoclouds and data center operators bearing some of the most painful losses.

Notably, AMD dropped 8% after the short-seller Hunterbrook revealed a new bet against the chip company. The short position was pegged to claims AMD could have business ties to IEIT Systems, a Chinese IT firm blacklisted by the US government last year.

An AMD spokesperson said the claims "misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships." The spokesperson added that the company complies with US export control laws and "maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations."

Nvidia, which has been at the center of market turmoil amid its leadership crisis, dropped 3%.

Here were some of the other notable moves in the AI sector:

NebiusNBIS-9%
Roundhill Neocloud ETFNCLD-6%
CoreWeaveCRWV-6%
IRENIREN-6%
VertivVRT-5%
AmazonAMZN-4%
SpaceXSPCX-4%
AlphabetGOOGL-4%
NvidiaNVDA-3%
MetaMETA-3%

There are a few things that explain the market's broader weakness:

Investors could be selling other stocks to buy Anthropic. Investors may be dumping other investments in order to free up capital, top economist Mohamed El-Erian wrote on X amid the selling.

"Investor financing of the mega-IPO involves making room by selling other holdings," he said.

Investors could be redirecting their attention back to the AI risk scenario. With Democrats in control of Congress, doubts have started to swirl around the future of data center construction in the US. Concerns about the massive amounts of debt being taken out to fund the AI buildout are also playing out in the background, Luke Lango, an independent tech analyst, wrote in a note.

"Nobody doubted demand for AI. What investors doubt is whether Washington, Wall Street, and the supply chain will let that demand get built at a price that makes sense," Lango said on Thursday. "A record IPO doesn't fix 5% Treasury yields, export controls, or circular financing, and it actually pulled $81 billion out of the rest of the AI trade to pay for itself."

"Is the AI investment cycle actually sustainable is the right question to be asking," Nancy Tengler, the chief investment officer at Laffer Tengler Investments, wrote in a note.

Fears of higher interest rates. Fed Governor Chris Waller called for a jumbo-sized rate hike when speaking to CNBC yesterday, fanning fears that interest costs will continue to rise amid Big Tech's borrowing spree.

Spillover from Nvidia. The market has been rattled lately by Nvidia's leadership crisis with Jensen Huang. Huang, who has served as an unofficial poster child for the AI trade, stepped down as CEO last week amid controversy related to his extramarital affairs, including one reported relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.

The exit is being seen by some in an existential light, given Nvidia's web of financing deals that have its success tied to every corner of the AI trade.

"AI sentiment continues to buckle," José Torres, a senior economist at Interactive Brokers, wrote in a client note. "The absence of former Nvidia CEO and hype-man Jensen Huang is also weighing upon the sector's outlook," he added.

The major indexes are moving further below their 200-day moving averages, a highly watched technical level, Torres said.

Anthropic's IPO is being viewed as a bellwether for the broader AI trade.

A weak market debut risks triggering a larger hit to stock prices across the AI sector, Alex Segal, a global equity analyst from Wells Fargo, wrote in a note.

"If the November 19 IPO is weak — including any disappointing demand or a sharp post-listing decline — investor confidence could suffer a new blow and trigger further valuation resets across AI-related equities," Sagal said.

"In many respects this IPO may mark a turning point in the AI space. The recent weakness of the infrastructure and semiconductor public companies could be understood as the market moving on from the early cycle of investment in compute at any cost," Gavin Ezekowitz, the chief investment officer at BFA Global Investors, wrote in a note on Thursday. The firm first invested in Anthropic when the Claude parent was valued at $17 billion.

Analysts are also bracing for more volatility around the stock.

Due to the extreme hype around Anthropic, the stock's pricing contains very little room for error, Kamran Ansari, a venture capital investor, said. He estimated even a small miss on financial forecasts could cause the stock to drop 10% down the line.

"Expect a pop, then a drop," Ansari wrote in a note. "If you price to perfection and squeeze out every cent, the stock has no room to run in the first few days of trading, something bankers fiercely try to avoid. Expect Anthropic to come back to Earth."

Even the largest IPO in history couldn't stop the AI trade from tumbling lower this week.

US stocks initially jumped on Thursday amid the massive hype for Anthropic's successful IPO and anticipation for the stock's first trades. The rally fizzled out by late morning, with the major indexes plunging into the afternoon as a broader risk-off move overpowered investors' excitement for a record-breaking IPO.

The Nasdaq 100 lost 2%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped as much as 1,100 points. The S&P 500 also lost more than 2% and notched its sixth straight losing session, marking the index's longest losing streak since 2024.

这是下午 4 点美国指数的走势。 东部时间收盘钟声：

  • S&P 500: 7,175.89, down 2.02%
  • Dow Jones Industrial Average: 49,097.77, down 2.19% (-1,100.40 points)
  • Nasdaq 100: 26,517.05, down 2.21%

Anthropic completed a record offering after the closing bell on Wednesday, raising $81 billion after increasing the number of shares it sold to investors. By total capital raised, the IPO beat out SpaceX's offering, which initially raised $75 billion.

Anthropic's stock, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, surged 34% at the open to $111.50 a share. The stock pulled back to trade around $97 a share by the closing bell, a 17% increase from its offering price of $83 a share.

Investors have used the IPO as an opportunity to take profits in other high-flying areas of the tech trade. In particular, traders are punishing AI names that have come under greater scrutiny lately amid the latest sell-off, with neoclouds and data center operators bearing some of the most painful losses.

Notably, AMD dropped 8% after the short-seller Hunterbrook revealed a new bet against the chip company. The short position was pegged to claims AMD could have business ties to IEIT Systems, a Chinese IT firm blacklisted by the US government last year.

An AMD spokesperson said the claims "misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships." The spokesperson added that the company complies with US export control laws and "maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations."

Nvidia, which has been at the center of market turmoil amid its leadership crisis, dropped 3%.

Here were some of the other notable moves in the AI sector:

我不会NBIS-9%
Roundhill Neocloud ETFNCLD-6%
CoreWeaveCRWV-6%
IRENIREN-6%
维谛技术VRT-5%
亚马逊AMZN-4%
太空探索技术公司SPCX-4%
字母GOOGL-4%
英伟达NVDA-3%
MetaMETA-3%

There are a few things that explain the market's broader weakness:

Investors could be selling other stocks to buy Anthropic. Investors may be dumping other investments in order to free up capital, top economist Mohamed El-Erian wrote on X amid the selling.

"Investor financing of the mega-IPO involves making room by selling other holdings," he said.

Investors could be redirecting their attention back to the AI risk scenario. With Democrats in control of Congress, doubts have started to swirl around the future of data center construction in the US. Concerns about the massive amounts of debt being taken out to fund the AI buildout are also playing out in the background, Luke Lango, an independent tech analyst, wrote in a note.

"Nobody doubted demand for AI. What investors doubt is whether Washington, Wall Street, and the supply chain will let that demand get built at a price that makes sense," Lango said on Thursday. "A record IPO doesn't fix 5% Treasury yields, export controls, or circular financing, and it actually pulled $81 billion out of the rest of the AI trade to pay for itself."

"Is the AI investment cycle actually sustainable is the right question to be asking," Nancy Tengler, the chief investment officer at Laffer Tengler Investments, wrote in a note.

Fears of higher interest rates. Fed Governor Chris Waller called for a jumbo-sized rate hike when speaking to CNBC yesterday, fanning fears that interest costs will continue to rise amid Big Tech's borrowing spree.

Spillover from Nvidia. The market has been rattled lately by Nvidia's leadership crisis with Jensen Huang. Huang, who has served as an unofficial poster child for the AI trade, stepped down as CEO last week amid controversy related to his extramarital affairs, including one reported relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.

The exit is being seen by some in an existential light, given Nvidia's web of financing deals that have its success tied to every corner of the AI trade.

"AI sentiment continues to buckle," José Torres, a senior economist at Interactive Brokers, wrote in a client note. "The absence of former Nvidia CEO and hype-man Jensen Huang is also weighing upon the sector's outlook," he added.

The major indexes are moving further below their 200-day moving averages, a highly watched technical level, Torres said.

Anthropic's IPO is being viewed as a bellwether for the broader AI trade.

A weak market debut risks triggering a larger hit to stock prices across the AI sector, Alex Segal, a global equity analyst from Wells Fargo, wrote in a note.

"If the November 19 IPO is weak — including any disappointing demand or a sharp post-listing decline — investor confidence could suffer a new blow and trigger further valuation resets across AI-related equities," Sagal said.

"In many respects this IPO may mark a turning point in the AI space. The recent weakness of the infrastructure and semiconductor public companies could be understood as the market moving on from the early cycle of investment in compute at any cost," Gavin Ezekowitz, the chief investment officer at BFA Global Investors, wrote in a note on Thursday. The firm first invested in Anthropic when the Claude parent was valued at $17 billion.

Analysts are also bracing for more volatility around the stock.

Due to the extreme hype around Anthropic, the stock's pricing contains very little room for error, Kamran Ansari, a venture capital investor, said. He estimated even a small miss on financial forecasts could cause the stock to drop 10% down the line.

"Expect a pop, then a drop," Ansari wrote in a note. "If you price to perfection and squeeze out every cent, the stock has no room to run in the first few days of trading, something bankers fiercely try to avoid. Expect Anthropic to come back to Earth."
